art01.title: Welcome to Arts GOZ Student Portal
art01.excerpt: Discover how the new GOZ student portal simplifies your academic and daily life at Faculty of Arts, Chula.
art01.author: Saraniyakorn Team
art01.content_0: We are proud to introduce the new Arts GOZ Student Portal. This platform is designed to be the central hub for all student services, academic tracking, and public relations.
art01.content_1: You can now easily track your curriculum progress, submit course petitions, download important documents, and keep up with campus events through our integrated calendar.
art01.content_2: Explore the various tabs and features. If you find any issues, feel free to submit feedback to help us improve the platform.

art02.title: How to Prepare for the Summer Internship Program
art02.excerpt: An ultimate guide on finding internships, building resumes, and preparing for interviews in your junior year.
art02.author: P'Siri, Arts 84
art02.content_0: Securing a summer internship is a great way to gain professional experience and explore career paths. Start by preparing your resume and showcasing your language skills.
art02.content_1: Many top companies offer roles in Content Marketing, UX/UI Design, and Localization for Arts students. Tailor your application for each role.
art02.content_2: Practice common interview questions and be confident in your multilingual capabilities. Good luck!

art03.title: WestCiv Survival Guide: Tips from Senior Students
art03.excerpt: Don't panic! Here are the best study techniques and reading recommendations to pass Western Civilization with an A.
art03.author: History Major Seniors
art03.content_0: Western Civilization (WestCiv) is known for its heavy reading load. The key is consistent reading and understanding the main historical themes rather than memorizing dates.
art03.content_1: Form study groups to discuss key concepts and summarize chapters. Sharing notes can help clarify complex historical events.
art03.content_2: Don't hesitate to ask your professors for guidance during office hours. They are always happy to help.

art04.title: Student Wellness: Managing Stress and Mental Health
art04.excerpt: Learn about the counseling services and wellness activities available to Chula students.
art04.author: GOZ Welfare Team
art04.content_0: Academic stress can take a toll on your mental health. Chulalongkorn University provides various support channels, including MindSpace and professional counseling.
art04.content_1: Remember to take breaks, practice mindfulness, and balance your study schedule with activities you enjoy.
art04.content_2: If you or your friends need someone to talk to, don't hesitate to reach out to the university's support services.

art05.title: The Evolution of Language in the Digital Era
art05.excerpt: Explore how social media, memes, and internet slang are shaping the future of Thai and English.
art05.author: Linguistics Club
art05.content_0: The digital era has accelerated the evolution of language. Internet slang, abbreviations, and emojis have become integral to modern communication.
art05.content_1: Linguists observe that these changes reflect social adaptation and the need for fast, expressive digital interaction.
art05.content_2: Understanding these trends helps us adapt communication strategies in both personal and professional contexts.

art06.title: Behind the Scenes of the Arts Open House 2026
art06.excerpt: Exclusive interviews with the student organizers who made this year's Open House a huge success.
art06.author: Saraniyakorn Reporter
art06.content_0: This year's Arts Open House attracted thousands of high school students. The event showcased the diversity of our majors and active student clubs.
art06.content_1: Organizers spent months planning interactive booths, campus tours, and mock classes to give prospective students a taste of life at Arts Chula.
art06.content_2: A big thank you to all student volunteers who dedicated their time to make this event successful and memorable.

faq.faq_1_question: What student services does GOZ offer, and where can I access them
faq.faq_1_answer: GOZ offers umbrella lending, free emergency sanitary pads, and basic first-aid medicines. Students can contact the GOZ room on Floor M1 of the Mahachakri Sirindhorn Building, Faculty of Arts, Monday–Friday from 09:00 E7:00.
faq.faq_2_question: How can I check the courses in the Faculty of Arts curriculum
faq.faq_2_answer: Students can go to the "Curriculum" tab on the main navigation bar to view required courses, electives, and credit details for different course groups in the latest Bachelor of Arts program directly.
faq.faq_3_question: What is the Academic Tracker feature, and how does it calculate credits
faq.faq_3_answer: Academic Tracker is a personal tool that allows students to record courses they have completed. The system will automatically calculate accumulated credits, separating faculty-required courses, major-required courses, and free electives to verify whether a student has met the graduation requirements.
faq.faq_4_question: What should I do when I find a system error or want to report a bug on the website
faq.faq_4_answer: If you find a bug or incorrect information, you can click the "Report Website Issue" button at the bottom of the homepage, or press the "Send Additional Questions" button to contact the developers directly.
faq.faq_5_question: How can I follow news and the Faculty's event schedule
faq.faq_5_answer: Students can follow along via the "Activity Calendar & Schedule" on the homepage, which shows dates and times of various events with status tags (e.g., Today, Tomorrow, Important, Don't Forget) so students won't miss any important events.

about.title: Faculty of Arts Student Committee (GOZ)
about.description: We are a student committee that facilitates academic resources, student welfare, and activities for Arts students. Our vision and policies for academic year 2025 are as follows:
vision_points: Organize activities that align more with the interests of students within the faculty, and increase external activities in collaboration with other faculties while preserving the unique identity of the Faculty of Arts.
Create a safe and comfortable working environment where members can communicate and express their opinions equally with open minds.
Serve as the hub and voice for the ultimate benefit of all Faculty of Arts students.
policy_points: Provide opportunities for students to express their opinions.
Represent and protect students' rights and welfare in the faculty.
Support organizing activities beneficial to students to prepare them for their future.
Prioritize the mental health of all GOZ members and Faculty of Arts students.

thai.title: Thai Language Major
thai.description: Deep dive into Thai language structures, literature, and culture. Focuses on critical literary analysis, linguistics, and creative communications.
thai.requirements: High school diploma or equivalent. Passionate about Thai language, classical and modern literature, and creative content creation.

english.title: English Major
english.description: Develops advanced English communication skills, critical analysis of Western literature, linguistics, and cultural studies. Tailored for global careers.
english.requirements: High school diploma or equivalent. Meets minimum English proficiency test score requirements as declared by the university.

history.title: History Major
history.description: Systematic study of Thai and world history. Learn how to critically analyze, interpret, and evaluate historical records and primary source materials.
history.requirements: High school diploma or equivalent. Passionate about historical research, archives, and possesses strong critical thinking skills.

geography.title: Geography & Geoinformatics Major
geography.description: Examines human-environment interactions through spatial analysis. Gain hands-on experience in GIS (Geographic Information Systems) and remote sensing.
geography.requirements: High school diploma or equivalent. Interested in maps, environmental studies, resource management, and computer geoinformatics.

philosophy.title: Philosophy Major
philosophy.description: Study Eastern and Western philosophical traditions. Focuses on critical thinking, ethical analysis, logic, and debates on contemporary global issues.
philosophy.requirements: High school diploma or equivalent. Enjoys reading, logical reasoning, and open-minded discussions on diverse points of view.

information.title: Information Studies Major
information.description: Study library sciences, information architecture, metadata curation, and data analytics to drive knowledge management in the digital age.
information.requirements: High school diploma or equivalent. Passionate about digital technologies, data curation, and organizational analytics.

french.title: French Major
french.description: Mastery of the French language, Francophone literature, and cultural history to foster careers in diplomacy, translation, and international trade.
french.requirements: High school diploma or equivalent. French language proficiency background as specified in university guidelines.

german.title: German Major
german.description: Deep study of German language systems, European history, and advanced communication skills tailored for global business and translation sectors.
german.requirements: High school diploma or equivalent. Strong interest in European languages, cultures, and global commerce.

japanese.title: Japanese Major
japanese.description: Advanced Japanese linguistics, modern literature, and historical studies designed for international corporate operations and cultural exchanges.
japanese.requirements: High school diploma or equivalent. Meets minimum Japanese language requirements or standardized test criteria.

chinese.title: Chinese Major
chinese.description: Acquire professional fluency in Chinese. Studies classical and modern literature, history, and economic relations in the East Asian region.
chinese.requirements: High school diploma or equivalent. Meets specified Chinese language test criteria as declared.

pali.title: Pali and Sanskrit Major
pali.description: Exploration of ancient Indo-Aryan languages, Buddhist scriptures, and comparative linguistics to research historical philosophies and heritage.
pali.requirements: High school diploma or equivalent. Passionate about classical linguistic structures, texts, and archeology.

spanish.title: Spanish Major
spanish.description: Fluency in Spanish alongside literature and social histories of Spain and Latin America. Prepares graduates for international development roles.
spanish.requirements: High school diploma or equivalent. Enthusiastic about global foreign languages and multilingual relations.

italian.title: Italian Major
italian.description: Mastery of Italian communication, art history, fashion industries, food cultures, and literature to build careers in creative industries.
italian.requirements: High school diploma or equivalent. Passionate about art history, European heritage, and creative design industries.

korean.title: Korean Major
korean.description: Focuses on Korean linguistics, modern media industries, pop cultures, and history. Prepares graduates for roles in international media and relations.
korean.requirements: High school diploma or equivalent. Standardized Korean proficiency test results as required.

arabic.title: Arabic Major
arabic.description: Mastery of Arabic language alongside cultural histories of the Middle East, preparing graduates for aviation, embassy, and corporate roles.
arabic.requirements: High school diploma or equivalent. Interested in Middle Eastern languages, history, and international relations.

south_asian.title: South Asian Languages Major
south_asian.description: Study of Hindi, regional histories, and Indian socio-political systems to enable trade, diplomacy, and cultural exchanges.
south_asian.requirements: High school diploma or equivalent. Passionate about commercial trade and relations in the South Asian region.

balac.title: Language and Culture (BALAC)
balac.description: International program focusing on cultural studies, critical media analysis, and comparative languages, tailored for global creative leadership.
balac.requirements: High school diploma or equivalent. Standardized English proficiency test scores (TOEFL, IELTS, CU-TEP) meeting faculty requirements.

reviews.title: Internship Reviews
reviews.excerpt1: I learned how to work in a truly professional environment. The supervisor was very kind and gave detailed guidance. The Japanese skills I studied were used every single day. Highly recommended for those wanting Japanese business experience.
reviews.excerpt2: A great experience. I got to practice speaking and writing Chinese in real situations. The main job was translating documents and communicating with Chinese clients.
reviews.excerpt3: I experienced real diplomatic work, which deepened my understanding of embassy operations and Spanish culture. My Spanish skills improved noticeably.
reviews.excerpt4: Great working atmosphere and friendly colleagues. I got to practice French writing to communicate with international clients.
reviews.excerpt5: So fun! I got to translate Korean subtitles and learn how the Korean entertainment industry works. My listening skills improved a lot.
reviews.excerpt6: I helped plan lessons and produce learning materials. This experience confirmed that I want to work in education.
